t: LeetCode 2129 - Capitalize the Title: Length-Ruled Casing
o: **Understanding the problem.** Words are separated by single spaces and contain only English letters; the casing of the input is arbitrary. A word of length 1 or 2 must become entirely lowercase, while longer words get an uppercase first letter with the rest lowercased. "capiTalIze tHe titLe" has only length-3-plus words and becomes "Capitalize The Title". In "First leTTeR of EACH Word" the two-letter word "of" stays fully lowercase while every other word is title-cased. In "i lOve leetcode" the one-letter word "i" remains lowercase while "lOve" becomes "Love". The tiny length limit (100 characters) means any straightforward string pass works; correctness hinges on applying the length rule per word.
k: Lowercase each word first, then conditionally uppercase its first character - this neutralizes messy input casing.
Length alone decides the rule: 1-2 letters stay all lowercase, 3+ letters get exactly one leading uppercase.
In-place two-pointer editing avoids building intermediate word lists.

a.i: Split the title on spaces, lowercase every word, and uppercase only the first letter of words longer than two characters. Joining with single spaces restores the title. This leans on language utilities and is the quickest to reason about.
s: Split title into words on single spaces.
If a word has more than 2 letters, uppercase its first character.
Join the words back together with single spaces and return.
a.t: O(n) over the title length - every character is normalized a constant number of times
a.sp: O(n) - for the word collection and the rebuilt string

a.i: Because words are delimited by single spaces, the buffer can be transformed directly: locate each word's boundaries with two indices, lowercase the whole span, then restore an uppercase first letter when the span exceeds two characters. No auxiliary word list is needed - relevant when allocations are restricted or the string is mutable.
s: Scan with i from 0; advance j to the next space or the end - the window [i, j) is one word.
If j - i > 2, uppercase the character at index i.
Continue from j + 1 until the string is exhausted.
a.t: O(n) - each character is visited once as part of exactly one word
a.sp: O(n) - a mutable copy is required except in C++, where the edit is truly in place

w: Default to split-normalize-rejoin; offer the in-place scan when asked to minimize allocations. Classic traps: leaving 1-2 letter words merely unchanged instead of forcing them lowercase, trusting built-ins like Python's str.title() that ignore the length rule, and breaking the guaranteed single-space separation when rejoining. Edge cases: a one-word title, already-correct input, and the short words "a" / "i". Follow-ups: punctuation-aware tokenization, or handling tabs and multiple spaces.
